timecoded_text_to_speech.text: It's time for the long-gene connoisseurs. The television journal of the important issues of the hour brought to you every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
A presentation of the long-gene Whitnor Watts Company, maker of long-gene, the world's most honored Watts, and Whitnor, distinguished companion to the world-honored long-gene.
Good evening, this is Frank Knight. May I introduce our co-editors for this edition of the long-gene chronoscope.

Mr. William Bradford Huey, author and analyst, and Mr. Hardy Bert, author and correspondent. Our distinguished guest for this evening is Dr. Howard Russ, chairman of the American Korean Rehabilitation Commission.
Dr. Russ, we're fortunate this evening in that you have just returned from Korea and you can give us a firsthand report on some of those interesting things there.
First of all, our viewers are most interested about the prospects of peace in the Orient, or how do you feel yourself about the prospects of a peaceful settlement?
Well, I am not an expert in that line, but it certainly is very heartening to me.
It seems to me that this is one step that we must make, and in my own heart I can't help but feel hopeful about it.
Well, sir, you, of course, are a famous doctor and one of the most famous people in the country regarding rehabilitation work because you've visited so many nations for our own country.
But first of all, sir, what can you tell our viewers about the medical care of our own GI's in Korea?
